title: Valid Sudoku
statement: You get a 9 by 9 board. Each cell holds a digit from 1 to 9 or a dot for empty. Check only the filled cells: no digit may repeat in a row, in a column, or in any of the nine 3 by 3 boxes. The board does not need to be solvable.

example.caption: The two 5s share the top-left 3 by 3 box. They share no row and no column, but the board is still invalid.

idea.sentence: Keep a set of seen digits for every row, every column and every box. A filled cell is fine only if its digit is in none of its three sets.

jargon.plain: A number 0 to 8 for the 3 by 3 box a cell sits in, counted left to right, top to bottom: floor(r/3)*3 + floor(c/3).
The cells that share a row, a column or a box with a given cell.

watch.inputHint: One argument: a 9 by 9 board of strings, dots for empty. Use the presets as a template.

compare.bruteLabel: Compare each cell with all its peers

rows.name: Brute force
rows.note: Compare every filled cell with every other filled cell and test if they are peers.

rows.name: Three families of sets
rows.note: Each filled cell does three lookups and three inserts. The 27 sets hold each digit three times at most.

fast.takeaway: The board is a fixed 9 by 9, so both are tiny in practice. The idea is what to learn: one set per row, column and box turns every rule into a lookup.

stages.title: 27 empty sets
stages.note: Nine sets for rows, nine for columns, nine for boxes. Each holds the digits seen there.

stages.title: Find the box
stages.note: A cell has a row r and a column c. Its box is floor(r/3)*3 + floor(c/3).

stages.title: Seen? Invalid
stages.note: If the digit is already in the row set, the column set or the box set, the board is invalid. After the last cell it is valid.

stages.title: Remember in all three
stages.note: Add the digit to its row set, its column set and its box set.

edges.title: Empty board
edges.why: Nothing is filled, so nothing can clash. Dots are skipped, never stored.

edges.title: Clash only in a box
edges.why: No shared row or column. Only the box set catches it.

edges.title: Same digit, diagonal boxes
edges.why: Different row, column and box. A wrong box formula such as r/3 + c/3 would put both in box 1 and fail this.

edges.title: Clash in the last cell
edges.why: The scan must reach the end. Stopping early on a small prefix of the board misses it.

gotchas.text: new Array(9).fill(new Set()) puts the same Set object in all nine slots. Every row would share one set. Use Array.from({ length: 9 }, () => new Set()).
Cells are strings. The dot is a string too. Compare with '.' and keep digits as strings in the sets. Do not mix 5 and '5'.
[9][9]bool arrays are zeroed values, so no setup is needed. Index the digit as board[r][c][0] - '1' to get 0 to 8. A dot must be skipped before that, or the byte math wraps around.
r/3 is integer division, so r/3*3 + c/3 needs no floor. In TypeScript the same expression needs Math.floor, because / gives a float.
Use one pass with all three checks. Three separate passes work too, but the box check is the one most often forgotten.

recap.pattern: Hash sets per row, column and box
recap.key: Each digit must be new in its row set, its column set and its box set. The box is floor(r/3)*3 + floor(c/3).
recap.complexity: Time O(81) = constant for a 9 by 9 board. Space O(81).
moves: Make 9 row sets, 9 column sets, 9 box sets
Reject if the digit is in its row, column or box set
Otherwise add it to all three
